The collapse of the ancient bridge serves as the inciting incident that disrupts the status quo, forcing the villagers to confront a critical survival challenge. This event drives the plot forward by shifting the narrative from passive dependence on external resources to active self-reliance. The resulting isolation catalyzes character and community development, as the villagers are compelled to demonstrate ingenuity and forge new paths. Ultimately, this crisis fosters unity and unexpected leadership, transforming the society into a more self-sufficient entity and setting the stage for future developments rooted in their newfound resilience and independence.

Regarding your question, the animal typically regarded as man's best friend is the dog.
